correctness.summary: The exact-CG threshold theorem checks. A-conjugacy gives r_k^T A p_k=p_k^T A p_k, so expansion of r_{k+1}=r_k-alpha_k A p_k yields the exact squared-ratio identity -1+||r_k||^2||A p_k||^2/(p_k^T A p_k)^2. The Kantorovich inequality contributes at most K^2=(L+mu)^2/(4Lmu), while r_k is orthogonal to p_{k-1}, giving d_k=||p_k||^2/||r_k||^2>=1 and d_k=1+beta_{k-1}d_{k-1}. Hence the all-step bound follows. For r_0=sqrt(L)u_mu+sqrt(mu)u_L the first step attains exactly (kappa-1)/(2sqrt(kappa)); solving when this is at most one gives kappa<=3+2sqrt(2), proving both sufficiency and necessity for uniform Euclidean-residual monotonicity. The fixed-SPD-preconditioner reformulation is ordinary CG on M^{-1/2}AM^{-1/2} and therefore has the same sharp threshold in the M^{-1} residual norm.

independent_checks: Re-derived the residual-ratio identity and applied the Kantorovich inequality directly.
Verified the endpoint two-eigenvector construction algebraically, including equality at kappa=3+2sqrt(2).
Inspected Meurant 2006 Chapter 2 pages 45-68 under authorized institutional access, including the complete residual-norm section through Proposition 2.8.
limitations: Finite-dimensional real SPD matrices and exact arithmetic only.
The PCG extension concerns the M^{-1} residual norm, not Euclidean PCG residuals.
The condition-number threshold is uniform over right-hand sides and starting guesses; individual runs can remain monotone above it.
Historical CG literature is large, so a differently phrased equivalent theorem remains a residual attribution risk despite direct inspection of the most relevant Meurant section.

literature_access.access: Authorized Oxford institutional access after open-access searching did not provide the complete chapter text.
literature_access.finding: The residual-norm section studies oscillation criteria and gives a coarse one-step bound ||r_{k+1}||/||r_k||<=1+kappa(A); no audited sharp 3+2sqrt(2) threshold or matching sharp factor was found before the text proceeds to error-norm analysis.

originality.summary: The classical literature already establishes highly nonmonotone CG residual histories and local criteria. The most directly relevant source, Meurant's 2006 Chapter 2, was obtained through authorized institutional access after open-access searching and the residual section was inspected through Proposition 2.8. It gives Lanczos-coefficient conditions for residual increase/decrease and Proposition 2.7's coarse bound ||r_{k+1}||/||r_k||<=1+kappa(A), but no fixed-matrix iff threshold 3+2sqrt(2), sharp all-step factor, or history certificate matching the audited result was found there. Brown's 2024 note gives a first-step vector criterion and a weaker sufficient condition from one endpoint mixture. Targeted searches likewise did not locate the audited sharp condition-number-only statement. Originality is therefore supported narrowly for the sharp uniform threshold/factor and history refinement.

scientific_value.summary: The theorem gives an exact condition-number boundary for a commonly monitored but nonmonotone CG quantity, with a matching worst-case construction for every fixed SPD matrix and an observable per-step refinement. It also transfers cleanly to fixed-preconditioner CG in the natural residual norm.
